chapter_title: What is Virginal; or, otherwise, what is Continent
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶3:** What is called *virginal* pertains to the interior mystery of the celestial degrees of the Divine order. And it is called *virginal* according to the quality of all that wisdom which never [GAP-1: REVIEW — the spiritual sense requires: was ever exposed to or received into itself any quality of] spiritual death, nor entered into the combat that falsity from evil wages against good.

**¶4:** However, what is called *continent* pertains to the mystery of that wisdom which descended and was conjoined with falsity from evil. It was contaminated in external natural states [GAP-2: — the spiritual sense requires a reference to the defilement through successive corporeal conditions] and afterward ascended toward interior illumination. [GAP-3: REVIEW — the spiritual sense requires: Those who perceived this quality of purified good] called it *continent*.

**¶5:** Furthermore, the holy states of untouched wisdom [GAP-4: — the spiritual sense requires a description of their essential nature or purity] should they ever be brought forth against the assault [GAP-5: — the spiritual sense requires: of falsity from evil, they would] never receive spiritual death into themselves, nor [GAP-6: — the spiritual sense requires: suffer any contamination or profanation].

**¶6:** On the other hand, what is called *continent* is that wisdom which was conjoined with falsity, was purified, ascended out of all natural and corporeal states, and was established in the celestial degrees of the Divine order. It is called *continent* because it had received into itself the concupiscence of self-love; but afterward was cleansed from it and [GAP-7: REVIEW — the spiritual sense requires: was restored to a state of] sanctification.

**¶7:** Furthermore, what is called *virginal* is that wisdom which was purified through the representative likeness of the Divine Mediator. It ascended and attained [GAP-8: REVIEW — the spiritual sense requires: the interior celestial states. It was] established in the likeness of divine goods and truths in their heavenly form.

**¶8:** Again, what is [GAP-9: REVIEW — the spiritual sense requires: designated as] *continent* is the remaining portion of that wisdom which was left behind from what had been purified. It passes through successive states of vastation and restoration in alternating cycles. Also, there is a part [GAP-10: REVIEW — the spiritual sense requires: belonging to] it that shall descend and enter the natural degree of the external man. Again, that portion too shall be regenerated while in the natural state, [GAP-11: REVIEW — the spiritual sense requires: receive into itself] the faith that proceeds from charity, and become sanctified. And this they call *continent*.

---

**Translator's note:** The distinction running through the entire passage is between two kinds of divine wisdom: one that never fell into conjunction with falsity (*virginal* — corresponding to celestial good that remains in its primordial integrity within the highest heavens), and one that descended into mixture with falsity and evil, suffered contamination in natural and corporeal states, but was afterward purified and restored (*continent* — corresponding to spiritual good that is regenerated through combat and cleansing). The *Ambassador* corresponds to the Lord in His mediating and revealing function, through whose Divine Human the higher kind of wisdom is liberated without contamination. The *transmigration* corresponds not to reincarnation in the natural sense, but to the successive states of vastation and illustration through which wisdom passes on its way from the natural degree back toward the celestial.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: What is called ‘virginal’ is assigned to the mystery of the aeons of greatness. And they called it ‘virginal’ by the category of all the light that did not [taste] of death, nor come to the enemy’s war.

However, what is called ‘continent’ occurs to the mystery of the light that came and was mixed with the darkness. It was defiled in bodies [and forms] and went up to the light. [They] called [it ‘co]ntinent’.
Furthermore, the holy vir[gin]als [are the lights that were not mixed with the darkness. And] should they come out against the en[emy in its war, they would not] taste death, nor [be defiled].

On the other hand, what is called ‘continent’ [is this li]ght that mixed with the darkness, was purif[ie]d, came [up f]rom all the creatures, and was confirmed in the great[ness]. They called it ‘continent’ since it tasted [of the l]ust; but afterwards was cleansed from it and [become an] holy one.
Furthermore, what is called [‘vi]rginal’ is this light that was purified by the ima[ge] of the [A]mbassador. It wen[t up and] attained [the] he[ights. It was] confirmed in the image of the gods.

Again, what is [called] ‘continent’ is the remainder of this light th[at] remained behind, from what was cleansed. It goes up and comes down in transmigration. Al[so], there is a part [of] it that shall come and attain the form of [hum]an [fl]esh. Again, that one too shall be chosen in the flesh, [accept] the hope, and become an holy one. And they name it ‘continent’.

fills.explanation: The phrase "taste of death" is a standard Manichaean-Kephalaia expression for receiving spiritual death into oneself; it perfectly conveys the spiritual sense of being exposed to or receiving the quality of spiritual death.
The pairing "bodies and forms" is standard Kephalaia vocabulary for successive corporeal conditions, matching the spiritual sense of defilement through multiple natural and external states.

The impersonal plural subject "They" corresponds to those who perceived this quality of purified good and gave it the designation "continent," consistent with the chapter's pattern of attributing names to perceivers of these categories.

fills.fill: are the lights that were not mixed with the darkness. And
fills.explanation: Structural parallelism with ¶6's definition of continent as "this light that mixed with the darkness" requires ¶5 to define the virginals as the opposite — unmixed light — and the conjunction transitions to the conditional clause.

fills.fill: emy in its war, they would not
fills.explanation: Completing "enemy" and echoing ¶3's "enemy's war," the conditional result clause leads naturally to "not taste death"; the structure is strongly constrained by the parallel in ¶3 and the bookending words "emy" and "not."

The spiritual sense requires "suffer contamination or profanation," and "be defiled" uses the same vocabulary as ¶4's "was defiled in bodies," creating the expected parallel for the virginal light that would never suffer such contamination.

The phrase "become an holy one" expresses restoration to a state of sanctification after cleansing, which matches the spiritual sense; the editor's reading is confirmed as the natural-register expression of being restored to sanctity.

The definite article "the" before "heights" is required to denote the specific interior celestial states to which the virginal light ascends, matching the spiritual sense of attaining the interior celestial degrees.

The formula "what is called" is the consistent pattern throughout the chapter (¶3, ¶4, ¶6, ¶7) for introducing the designation of each category, and "called" matches the spiritual sense of "designated as."
The preposition "of" expressing partitive belonging ("a part of it") is the standard construction for denoting a portion belonging to the whole, matching the spiritual sense of "belonging to."

The verb "accept" for receiving the hope (faith proceeding from charity) fits the spiritual sense of "receive into itself" and is consistent with the Kephalaia's vocabulary for the voluntary reception of spiritual goods in the natural state.
